Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

force noun

strength, violence

also by force, use force, violence, forcibly, forces, be in force

classical

Cic. Mil. 9: cum vī vīs illāta dēfenditur (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 1.14: per vim (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 317

vīs, vīs f.

noun, third declension: accusative vim, ablative vī; plural vīrēs, strength

force, violence; strength

vī or per vim, by force; vim adhibēre, to use force; vim afferre alicui, to do violence to someone (Lewis & Short). The force of wind or water is vīs too. Armed forces are cōpiae.

Examples

  • Ratiōne, nōn vī vincenda adulēscentia est.

    youth is to be won over by reason, not by forcePublil. Sent. R 14

  • Nōlī vim adhibēre; operculum suā sponte sequētur.

    Don’t force it: the lid will come off by itself.composed

  • vim adhibēre

    to use forceTraupman 317

  • valēre

    to be in force (of laws)Traupman 317

See also strength, force.
